transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2026-05-26 10:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Liu (Redwood AE), Sofia Gomez (Redwood SE), James Carter (BlueOak Head of ML), Priya Singh (Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (SRE)

[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone thanks for hopping on um we'll try to keep this to 45, afternoon schedule for some folks so appreciate it
[00:12] James: yep thanks Ethan, quick context from our side after the Friday incident, we saw a spike of 5xxs and elevated tail latency around 11:42 PST, about a 20 minute window where near real-time features degraded
[00:25] Sofia: got it, and that was during the batch of synthetic traffic from our internal load tests?
[00:31] James: sort of, it was yesterday we had a batch job plus organic traffic, so combined QPS jumped about 3x from baseline
[00:42] Priya: i can confirm the load pattern, our autoscaler didn't kick fast enough, and we also hit a rate-limit at the gateway that produced 429s which then cascaded into retries from the client
[00:55] Liam: and those retries looked like they were aggressive - client retried immediately which saturated the pool and then timeouts and 5xx followed, so a retry storm basically
[01:10] Ethan: ok that aligns with the logs we were sent last night, there was a mix of 429, 504 and some 500s. we also saw a KV cache churn - some of the prefix cache misses caused longer model cold-starts
[01:25] James: mhm some of the model variants were swapped too, we had a canary that fell back to a heavier model which increased latency further
[01:38] Sofia: that's important - fallback to heavier model + cache miss is a double whammy. quick question - which model variants were active during the window? do you have the mapping?
[01:50] Priya: i think default was redwood-v2-medium and the fallback was redwood-v2-large, but i will confirm in the logs
[02:02] Ethan: perfect, if you can include that in the export that helps. okay quick run through of what we saw on infra side: our observations - gateway rate-limit hit, client retries without jitter/backoff, kv cache miss, fallback to large model, autoscaler lag
[02:20] James: yeah that sums it up. we also noticed a surge of long-context requests which amplified KV cache pressure
[02:32] Sofia: makes sense. for immediate mitigations we typically recommend: reduce client-side retry aggressiveness, add exponential backoff with jitter, enable circuit-breaker on 5xxs, and temporarily increase rate-limit quota or provision dedicated capacity for the window
[02:48] Liam: curious about the circuit-breaker thresholds - what's Redwood's recommendation?
[02:54] Sofia: typical starting point is open after 5 errors within 30s for a route, then cool-down for 60s, but that depends on baseline QPS. we can provide tuned defaults based on your traffic profile
[03:10] Priya: can you quantify the overhead of enabling circuit-breaker? will it add latency to every request?
[03:18] Sofia: no, circuit-breaker is lightweight. it's basically a fast check in the request path; the cost is negligible compared to model inference. the upside is it prevents retry storms from further impacting healthy capacity
[03:30] James: ok good. next, about rate-limits - do you support dynamic per-customer quotas we can adjust during peak windows?
[03:39] Ethan: yes, Redwood supports dynamic routing and per-customer quotas. for POC we can temporarily raise your quota or stand up a dedicated pool for the benchmark window
[03:48] James: raising quota is fine as a short term fix, but we want to test the dedicated pool too to see unit-cost tradeoffs
[03:56] Sofia: we recommend a 2-hour dedicated run at representative QPS; we can provision reserved capacity and pin to the same model variant to avoid fallbacks
[04:10] Liam: ok great. on telemetry - we want end-to-end tracing correlation IDs. we sent you a sample trace id in the ticket, any update?
[04:20] Ethan: we received the sample, Sofia looked at it and there were some mismatched span names due to client SDK version, that's probably why some traces didn't join. Sofia?
[04:28] Sofia: yeah i saw that, your client was on 1.2.0 and the SDK mapping changed in 1.3.0 so some spans didn't propagate. upgrade will give cleaner traces; we'll attach a small patch and mapping doc
[04:42] Priya: ok we can schedule that upgrade during off-peak, maybe next Tuesday?
[04:48] James: timeline wise, we're trying to stabilize before the Friday batch tests next week
[04:54] Ethan: understood. for the bench run we suggest week of 6/1, ideally Monday morning to avoid batch jobs overlap
[05:05] James: Monday works.
[05:10] Sofia: quick note on retries - can you confirm what the client retry policy is now? jitter? exponential?
[05:18] Priya: currently it's immediate retry up to 3 attempts with 200ms fixed delay, so no jitter and small backoff
[05:26] Sofia: that's the issue. immediate retries + no jitter leads to synchronized retries. change to exponential backoff 100ms then x2 with +/- 30% jitter is safer
[05:38] Liam: we'll change that in the client. also we'll add server-side quota bubbling to return a more explicit header so clients can back off earlier
[05:46] Ethan: nice. ok let's talk about the 5xxs breakdown - from our side it's ~60% 504 gateway timeouts, ~25% 500 model errors, ~15% 429 rate-limit responses that led to retries
[06:01] James: that matches our counts roughly. model errors - some are memory OOMs when the large variant spawned, which indicates cold-start resource pressure
[06:11] Sofia: do you have the payload size distribution? long contexts cause model memory growth; quantization helps but heavy models still need headroom
[06:21] Priya: median context is 1.2k tokens but tail hits 12k occasionally during doc ingest jobs
[06:28] Sofia: tail is the problem. for those heavy requests we suggest segregating into a dedicated long-context route with stricter rate-limits and pre-warmed capacity
[06:40] James: ok sensible. we can do route tagging on our side to mark long-context requests
[06:46] Ethan: i'll add that to action items - send a sample tagging plan
[06:50] James: also curious about caching - you mentioned KV cache churn, can you explain how that manifests?
[06:56] Sofia: yes. the runtime uses prefix/KV caching for decoder KV keys. when many different prefixes hit, the cache thrashes and more GPU work happens, plus cold-starts if the model variant changes. reducing model variance and increasing cache retention helps
[07:12] Priya: any quick config we can change now? increase cache size? longer TTLs?
[07:18] Sofia: we can bump the prefix cache TTL for the pilot and pin the model variant. caching parameters are adjustable per-deployment, we'll propose numbers after seeing the logs
[07:28] Liam: how about rate-limit thresholds - default was 800 rps and we saw 2.4k during the spike. can you handle that if we provision dedicated pool?
[07:37] Ethan: yes with dedicated capacity we can handle sustained 2.5k rps depending on model size. we'll size the pool for target latency SLOs and share estimated cost
